notes: REWRITE of draft #35, written fresh; no numbers reused from the old draft (the old horsepower-to-pipe-size and ground-clearance rules of thumb are gone). Direct page fetches were blocked in this environment, so every fact came from WebSearch result summaries, mostly on the maker's own domain: Rogue Fab (3.0D / wall-ratio-20 mandrel guidance, mild steel at .083" or heavier bends cleanly for most exhaust work, the attachment's 'wall ratios over 30 and tighter than 2.5D not likely possible' note, 'not worth it for a single project', ram benders being repair-shop tools), Burns Stainless (no air gap, low-amp fused tacks, argon purge with stoppers at about 5 SCFH shield / 10 SCFH purge), Vibrant (1D 90s and U-J bends in 1.5"-4"), Stainless Headers (J-bends with 6" and 12" legs, plus the line that extra leg length removes the need for straight tube in most header builds). The 1/4" fit-up trim allowance comes from the Stainless Headers J-bend optimizer, as recorded in the site fact-check notes. 16 gauge = .065" wall is taken from Khaos (Amazon clp/B08R42HM7C title '.065 16ga') and the Stainless Headers 1-3/4" 16ga tubing listing. DNA ZTL-25SS: the Amazon listing gives 18-gauge T-304, 4 x 48" straights plus 4 each of 45/90/180, and expanded ends. The search summary said some other retailers describe the same kit as 16-gauge, which I could not open, so the article says 'per listing' and flags the gauge. Kit CLR was not visible, so the article says 'check the listing'. Vibrant 2609 specs come from the Amazon listing title (2.50" OD, 16 ga, 304, 3.50" CLR, 7.00" legs). Wall factor (~38 for 2.5" x .065"), D (~1.4 for 3.5" CLR) and the 45-degree arc example (2.75" centerline, 3.73" outside, 1.77" inside) are my own arithmetic. Left out as unverifiable: flow-loss or ovality percentages for crush bends, pipe-diameter-by-horsepower rules, ground-clearance numbers, and labor-time estimates.
